thread:
olivia: Heads-up — during the base-image rebuild this afternoon the keystore operator will need an extra permission to unwrap v2 envelopes. I want to avoid a canary failure. Anyone on-call for keystore RBAC?

alex: I can take this. what's the exact permission?

olivia: The operator currently has `kms.decrypt` on projects/rebuild-keystore. New envelope format uses envelope:v2 which requires `kms.asymmetricDecrypt` on the signing key resource.

mike: Wait, `asymmetricDecrypt` is only on the signer key. Are we rotating keys for the rebuild?

olivia: Yes — as part of the rebuild we rotate the signing key to the new attestation-protection key. That means the operator pod will need short-lived access to the new key (not the old symmetric one).

jana: How short-lived? Can we grant it via Workload Identity with a token-exchange role instead of static IAM binding?

alex: Prefer that. Proposal: create a dedicated service account `sa-keystore-unwrapper@redwood-prod` with a time-limited binding to the KMS key via a condition on `request.time` + an annotation on the pod. Then the operator uses Workload Identity to impersonate `sa-keystore-unwrapper` only when annotated.

luke-sre: Sounds safer. Two operational questions: 1) How will audit logs show the unwrap events (so SOC can triage)? 2) If the operator fails to unwrap in the canary, what's the fallback?

olivia: For audit we want structured entries forwarded to Splunk/BigQuery with fields: `actor`, `key_id`, `envelope_version`, `image_digest`. I've drafted a little log patch that adds structured metadata to the unwrap path.

sec-bot: Automated note — related CVE flags: none currently for the keystore operator, but image rebuild will bump `libseccomp` and `openssl`. Please watch vuln scan.

alex: Pasting the RBAC snippet I want to apply (will gate with a rollout):

```yaml
# grant only asymmetricDecrypt with a time-limited condition
bindings:
  - role: roles/cloudkms.publicKeyViewer
    members:
      - serviceAccount:sa-keystore-unwrapper@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  - role: roles/cloudkms.asymmetricDecrypter
    members:
      - serviceAccount:sa-keystore-unwrapper@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
    condition:
      title: "short-lived-unwrap"
      expression: "request.time < timestamp('2026-05-01T18:30:00Z')"
```

mike: That condition timestamp looks like a one-off. We'll need the CI job to patch it each rollout. Can we instead require the pod-level annotation: `iam.gke.io/allow-unwrap: 'true'`? Role conditions don't inspect pod annotations.

jana: You can emit an OAuth token via STS with a signed JWT that includes the pod annotation as claim, then a short-lived grant is issued. It's more complex but auditable.

luke-sre: For canary fallback: if operator can't unwrap, the canary build should fallback to serving the prebuilt fallback image from the fallback registry. We should implement the check as a simple healthprobe that verifies unwrap success within 45s.

olivia: +1 on fallback. Also we need the security review board to sign off on the audit fields retention — SOC asked for 365d retention for unwrap events. That affects cost and our retention policy.

alex: Operational plan I will run: 1) create `sa-keystore-unwrapper` and Workload Identity mapping, 2) add token exchange path in operator (JWT -> STS -> short token), 3) add structured audit metadata, 4) deploy to staging canary with `--replicas=1`, 5) smoke test unwrap and fallback.

mike: Who owns step 2? I can slot time this afternoon.

alex: Thanks — assign to @mike. @olivia please send the exact JWT claim format.

olivia: Will do. Quick log example to make sure Splunk parsers are ready: 

```json
{"ts":"2026-03-23T17:02:12Z","actor":"sa-keystore-unwrapper@redwood-prod","key_id":"projects/rebuild-keystore/locations/global/keyRings/base/cryptoKeys/attest-key","envelope_version":"v2","image_digest":"sha256:abc123","status":"success"}
```

jana: For the vuln triage — I'll run the rebuild image through the private scanner and post results here before you flip the key. If anything high comes up we block rotation.

sec-bot: Reminder: open incident template available if unwrap failures exceed 5% over 10 minutes: /incidents/template/keystore_unwrap_failure

luke-sre: I'll add the healthprobe check and the fallback marker to the canary helm chart. Planning to cut the canary at 18:00 PT.

olivia: Thanks team. If anyone hits permission denial logs like `google.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricDecrypt.permissionDenied`, ping me immediately and don't escalate the rollout.

alex: Noted. I'll push the RBAC change to a branch and request a short security review.

mike: On it — will update here when token-exchange PR is ready.

olivia: closing loop — will file a short runbook snippet after canary is green. :thumbsup:
